subject: DPA negotiation: subprocessor notification windows, objection matrix, and eSign path

Cc: Arcadia Legal <legal@arcadia-analytics.com>, Arcadia Procurement <procurement@arcadia-analytics.com>
Date: Sat, 21 Nov 2026 13:07:00 -0800
Subject: Arcadia DPA redline + subprocessor list — initial ask

Hi Markus / Karthik,

Thanks again for the demo earlier this week. Attached are two items from our side to keep the contract moving: 1) Arcadia_DPA_Redline.docx (our legal team’s edits to the standard DPA) and 2) Arcadia_Subprocessor_List.xlsx (current list + sensitivity classification).

Two items we’d like to resolve before signing:
- Notification window for new subprocessors (we're asking for 30 days prior notice).
- Objection process: we want a defined timeline and escalation path if we object to a subprocessor.

We'd also like to confirm whether Redwood prefers DocuSign or AdobeSign for execution. Procurement prefers DocuSign but legal can accommodate either. Could you please share Redwood's preferred flow and any suggested redlines on our doc?

Appreciate a quick turnaround — procurement would like to close by the end of the month.

Thanks,
Samantha Jones
Head of IT Procurement
Arcadia Analytics

Attachments: Arcadia_DPA_Redline.docx (docx), Arcadia_Subprocessor_List.xlsx (xlsx)

From: Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.com>
To: Samantha Jones <samantha.jones@arcadia-analytics.com>

Date: Mon, 23 Nov 2026 09:22:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Arcadia DPA redline + subprocessor list — initial ask

Samantha — thanks for sending this over and for the clear asks. We reviewed the attachments. High level response:

- eSign: Redwood uses DocuSign as our operational default for commercial agreements; we can accept Arcadia’s execution via DocuSign envelope.
- Notification window: Redwood standard is 45 days for non-critical subprocessors and 30 days for routine infrastructure changes. For processors handling sensitive identifiers we typically request 45 days plus a short technical summary.
- Objection process: we propose a two-step objection timeline: a 14-day review window after notification where Arcadia must submit specific grounds, followed by up to 15 business days for remediation/mitigation or removal evaluation. If unresolved, the parties can invoke escalation to security leads for a final 30-day cure period.

I’m attaching a counter-redline with our proposed language for the subprocessor notification / objection sections. Laura, Priyom — please weigh in on the exact language (I’ve highlighted the notice vs. objection timeline).

Markus Klein
Head of Sales, Redwood Inference

Attachment: Redwood_DPA_Counter_redline_v2.docx (docx)

From: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
To: Samantha Jones <samantha.jones@arcadia-analytics.com>, Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.com>

Date: Tue, 24 Nov 2026 11:03:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Arcadia DPA redline + subprocessor list — initial ask

Hi Samantha / team — quick legal note on the objection and notification mechanics. 

We reviewed Arcadia’s redline and propose the following practical language to avoid operational ambiguity:
1) Notification: Redwood will provide written notice (email + portal posting) no less than 45 calendar days for additions of subprocessors that will process Personal Data classified as Sensitive. For non-Sensitive processors, Redwood will provide notice no less than 30 calendar days.
2) Objection: Arcadia must provide a written notice of objection within 14 calendar days of receipt of notice, including a description of the objection and the specific contractual or regulatory basis.
3) Remediation/Cure: Redwood will have up to 15 business days to propose and implement reasonable mitigations. If Arcadia reasonably demonstrates that the mitigations are insufficient and the parties cannot agree, either party may terminate data processing for the impacted service area without penalty on 30 days’ notice.

We prefer DocuSign for final execution as Mark noted. For the redline changes, I propose the following: convert broad veto rights into a limited objection right tied to regulatory compliance or data residency concerns (this protects both parties operationally).

If Arcadia is comfortable with the above, we can prepare an execution-ready DPA and initiate the DocuSign envelope.

Best,
Laura Bennett
Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference

Laura/Markus — thanks for the clarity. A couple of follow-ups from legal/procurement before we move to execution: 

- Is email + portal posting sufficient notice for Arcadia or do you require certified delivery for higher-risk processors?
- Our procurement team requests a 30-day objection window (not 14). Can you explain the operational reasons for 14 days?
- Can you confirm the mutual action plan timeline so Procurement can clear the spend — we need the DocuSign envelope in our system by 29 Nov to meet vendor onboarding dates.

If we can align on notice method and the objection window, procurement will sign off and we’ll accept DocuSign.

Samantha

Subject: Re: Arcadia DPA redline + subprocessor list — initial ask

Samantha — quick privacy/ops response and proposed mutual action plan (MAP):

1) Notice method: Email to both technical-contact and procurement plus posting in the customer portal and a one-off in-app banner for the impacted feature. For high-risk processors (Sensitive data), we will also send certified delivery upon request.

2) Objection window: The 14-day window is meant to ensure timely review and avoid operational blocking for short-lived infra changes. That said, we understand procurement timelines. Proposal: Arcadia gets a 30-calendar-day formal objection window for initial notification (to align with your procurement), with an operational review period of 14 days for our engineering team to propose mitigations. Practically: Arcadia notifies within 30 days if you object; within the first 14 days Redwood will provide an engineering mitigation plan; then the remaining 16 days can be used by Arcadia to evaluate whether mitigations are acceptable before escalating.

3) MAP (dates relative to DocuSign envelope):
- 27 Nov: Finalize DPA redline (this week).
- 29 Nov: Redwood sends DocuSign envelope (we will use DocuSign).
- 30 Nov - 06 Dec: Arcadia internal review & signature (target).
- Post-signature: subprocessor notifications will follow the agreed windows above.

We can also include a short appendix in the DPA describing the subprocessor classification and the on-notice mitigation options (encryption, dedicated tenancy, SOC 2 evidence).

Link to DocuSign envelope (preview): https://docusign.com/envelopes/ABC123-Arcadia-DPA

Happy to jump on a 20-min call if helpful.

Thanks,
Priyom Das
Privacy Lead, Redwood Inference

- Please add the short appendix describing mitigation options for sensitive subprocessors (encryption, isolated tenancy, SOC 2 evidence).

If you can confirm those two items in the DPA we’ll proceed to signature today via the DocuSign link.

Samantha
